messages:
sasha: Quick heads-up — after converting MistralX-7B to our int4 pipeline with the new 'soft-alias' vocab mapping, evals show a measurable quality drop vs gemma4b baseline. Not huge but reproducible on the summarization suite.

rahul: numbers? repro steps?

sasha: Minimal repro: run `eval/run_qa.py --model mistralx-int4-softalias --suite summarization_small` — avg rouge-L down ~2.8 points, exact-match for short-answer down 4%. Sample diff: 
```
PROMPT: "Summarize: A doctor walked into the room and..."
BASELINE (gemma4b-fp16): "The doctor entered, checked vitals, and explained..."
MISTRALX-INT4-SOFTALIAS: "A dr entered and the patient was..."  <-- shorter, hallucinated filler
```

jean: soft-alias meaning we map multiple surface forms to a single token id to save vocab slots, right? Could be losing case sensitivity or punctuation anchors. Do we keep alias metadata at inference time?

sasha: Exactly — alias map merges rarer capitalized forms into lowercase main token at convert-time. The conversion tool currently strips the alias metadata and writes only the canonical id into `vocab.bin`. At decode time we lose the signal for word boundaries in some cases.

maya: Hmm. That could affect subword-prefix scoring and beam selection. Can you paste a quick token id diff for the sample?

sasha: pasted small snippet of the tokenizer IDs for the prompt: 
```
# gemma-fp16 tokens: [134, 22, 905, 78, 11]
# mistralx-int4-softalias tokens: [134, 22, 999, 78, 11]  # 905 -> 999 mapped
```

ci-bot: Build 2026.03.10-96 completed for mistralx-int4-softalias. Deployed to staging.

rahul: Try toggling alias handling at decode: `--alias-policy=strict|soft`. If strict preserves separate ids we should see metric recovery. Can you run `alias_policy=strict` on staging?

sasha: Ran it. Strict recovers ~1.9 rouge-L but introduces small OOV spikes (rare tokens now get unknowns). So tradeoff between hallucination vs OOV. Full results attached in staging job 96.

jean: Could also try emitting alias markers in logits post-processing: keep canonical id for embedding lookup but record a small learned bias for alias surface forms that nudges beam scoring. Less invasive than strict mapping.

maya: Agreed. Also check kv-cache alignment: if aliasing changed token lengths downstream we might be shifting attention positions. Any sign of off-by-one in longcontext runs?

sasha: Good call — I ran longcontext pass (4k) and saw a tiny attention drift where the next-token probs for repeated named entities diverge after 512 tokens. Suspect alias->id folding altered position tokenization fairly early.

rahul: Plan: 1) add a repro harness that compares soft vs strict vs postproc-bias on the summarization and chat suites, 2) add a unit test that ensures conversion preserves an alias manifest JSON alongside `vocab.bin`, 3) try a small learned bias prototype. I'll spin up jobs.

sasha: I'll open a PR with the conversion flag `--emit-alias-manifest` and an example script `tools/alias_postproc.py` that applies the bias table at decoding. Assigning to @jean for review.

jean: Sounds good, leave a short test that checks sample prompt outputs match expected tokenization for canonical vs alias forms. :thumbsup:

maya: If you need dedicated hardware for bisect runs ping me — can schedule a 2-hour block.

sasha: @maya appreciated — may take you up on that. I'll post a short summary in eng-ml once PR is up.

jean: Also add a tiny eval case where casing matters (e.g., 'US' vs 'us') — caught similar before.

sasha: Will do. Thanks all.
